name: Kessav Ube-Tamarind Gummies
manufacturer: Kessav Candy Group (Tier 2 mass market brand)
description: Standard synth-gelatin gummies in ube-tamarind flavor, molded into geometric shapes and sold in resealable pouches. A reliable, mid-range gummy with a flavor combination that's been in continuous production for eleven years.
flavor_profile: Sweet, earthy ube purple yam flavor with a tart tamarind sour note that sharpens toward the finish; the gummy texture is firm with a clean chew; no lingering aftertaste
cultural_context: Kessav ube-tamarind gummies have been around long enough that they feel permanent — a fixture of Tier 1 and 2 convenience shops that nobody thinks about until they're gone. The resealable pouch is frequently cited in consumer surveys as the product's best feature. Nobody is passionate about them, but almost everyone has eaten them.
story_hooks: Kessav is discontinuing the ube-tamarind line after eleven years to make room for a new SKU — the announcement has sparked a surprisingly emotional community response on public nets

A the Gray Zone community organizer has been using Kessav pouch reseal strips as a low-tech tamper indicator on food packages distributed to families in need — someone has figured this out and started compromising them
A child in the Gray Zone is found with a Kessav pouch that contains something that is definitively not gummies — and the pouch seal is intact
